title: Breast ultrasound
what: The doctor checks your breasts and armpits with ultrasound. It is safe, uses no radiation, and is fine at any age.
why: For a lump or pain in the breast, nipple discharge, as a checkup, or together with a mammogram.
tell_doctor: The first day of your last period
If you have felt a lump, and exactly where
If you have had breast surgery or have implants
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: If you have periods, it is best to come in the first half of your cycle, usually on day 5 to 12. After menopause, any day is fine.

prepare.title: Urgent
prepare.text: If you notice a lump or discharge, do not wait for the right cycle day. Book right away.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable that is easy to take off above the waist.

bring: Past ultrasounds and mammograms, to compare
steps: You undress to the waist and lie on your back
You put your arm behind your head
The doctor puts on gel and checks each breast
The armpits are checked separately. The lymph nodes are there
feel: The probe presses a little. It does not hurt
after: You can go back to your day straight away
You usually get the report right away
If something is found, the doctor may suggest a mammogram or a follow-up scan later

faq.q: On which day of my cycle should I have a breast ultrasound?
faq.a: Usually on day 5 to 12. The breasts are softer then, and the doctor can see better.

faq.q: Which is better, ultrasound or a mammogram?
faq.a: They work together. Under 40, ultrasound is used more often. Over 40, a mammogram, sometimes both. The doctor decides.

faq.q: Can I have a breast ultrasound while breastfeeding?
faq.a: Yes. It is best to feed or pump before the scan.

faq.q: How often should I have a breast ultrasound?
faq.a: Ultrasound is harmless and can be repeated. If everything is normal — usually once a year. If there are deviations — every six months. With benign lumps such as a fibroadenoma — every 3–6 months. A breast specialist will tell you the exact schedule.

reminders.text: Breast ultrasound tomorrow. Bring your past ultrasounds and mammograms.
